extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists, psychologists, and humor researchers conducting or evaluating fMRI studies of verbal humor
extracted.subtask_short: fMRI study of verbal humor processing
extracted.subtask_description: Experimental and theoretical framework for distinguishing and measuring incongruity-resolution versus absurd (nonsense) verbal humor using behavioral ratings and fMRI; includes stimulus design, acquisition/processing protocols, and hypothesized neural circuits. Useful for designing, evaluating, or replicating neuroimaging studies of verbal humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-stage model of humor processing (detection–resolution–elaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor comprehension occurs in three stages: incongruity detection, incongruity resolution, and elaboration (affective stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model focuses mainly on incongruity-resolution humor: detection supported by MTG and MFG activity; resolution supported by SFG and IPL (reestablish/ reinterpret setup and punch line); elaboration (feeling of pleasure) supported by vmPFC, bilateral amygdala, and bilateral PHG. The stages map to distinct psychological and neural subprocesses and motivate behavioral ratings (surprise, comprehensibility, funniness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-path model distinguishing incongruity-resolution vs absurd humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Extends the three-stage model: both humor types go through detection, resolution, and elaboration but via different subprocesses and neural circuits (a 'dual-path' account).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incongruity-resolution humor: complete resolution via semantic integration, perspective taking and episodic memory elaboration (stronger amusement). Absurd humor: partial/pseudo-resolution relying on phonological/semantic word processing and pragmatic meta-comprehension with residual absurdity (weaker amusement). The model predicts different brain areas per stage (see neural mapping metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Incongruity-resolution humor (INS-RES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes where the punch line violates a script/expectation formed by the setup but can be fully resolved by reinterpreting perspective and integrating contextual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution involves switching to the protagonist's perspective, integrating setup and punch line, and possible elaboration on protagonist traits (derogation, superiority). Example: 'Student: No. I was standing on it.' Neural correlates implicated: TPJ, precuneus, PCC, PHG, MTG, MFG, IPL, SFG. Expected behavioral pattern: higher surprise and funniness than absurd or neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Absurd (nonsense) humor (ABS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor containing incongruities that are illogical or impossible in reality so that incongruities can only be partially resolved (pseudo-resolution), leaving residual absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial resolution proceeds via phonological/semantic/word-level processing; pragmatic awareness/meta-comprehension interprets residual incongruity. Example: 'A margarine...becomes a butterfly.' Neural correlates: fusiform gyrus, lingual gyrus, IFG, STG. Expected behavioral pattern: lower surprise and funniness than incongruity-resolution but higher than neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolvability as classifier (complete vs partial/pseudo-resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which an incongruity can be resolved (complete resolution vs partial/pseudo-resolution) is the central distinguishing criterion between humor types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete resolution: semantic integration, perspective taking, coherence building, and elaboration leading to stronger amusement. Partial/pseudo-resolution: linguistic/phonological processing and pragmatic meta-comprehension leave residual absurdity and evoke weaker amusement or confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral measurement dimensions: surprise, comprehensibility, funniness
rubrics_metrics.description: Three types of ratings developed to reflect the three stages of humor processing: surprise (detection), comprehensibility (resolution), and funniness (elaboration/appreciation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-scan ratings used a four-point Likert scale; post-scan ratings used 1–9 scales for surprise, comprehensibility, and funniness. High correlations between in-scan and post-scan measures were reported (r ≈ 0.82–0.88). Interpret patterns: INC-RES > ABS > NEU in funniness; INC-RES and ABS > NEU in surprise; comprehensibility differences may be small/non-significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus design — two-part verbal stimuli (setup and punch line) and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Each stimulus comprises a setup and a punch line; neutral stimuli created by rewriting punch lines of humorous stimuli to be unfunny while preserving linguistic characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setup lengths ~39–42 words; punch line lengths ~10–11 words. Maintain close matching across conditions (INS-RES, ABS, NEU) for word counts and other text characteristics to ensure activation differences reflect humor mechanisms rather than linguistic differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus linguistic control using CRIE (Chinese Readability Index Explorer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an established readability tool (CRIE with 31 indices across word, semantic, syntax, and cohesion levels) to assess and confirm no significant linguistic differences across stimulus types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform statistical tests (e.g., one-way ANOVA) on CRIE indices and only proceed when no significant differences are found so neural differences can be attributed to humor mechanisms rather than text features. Appendix contains means/SDs and significance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection and sample size per condition
rubrics_metrics.description: After filtering, select a balanced set of stimuli per condition (here: 12 texts per stimulus type, total 48).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources: validated joke database (e.g., Cheng et al., 2013). Use pre-existing norming (e.g., funniness ratings) to ensure stimuli fall in intended ranges (reported means and SDs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental timing and presentation paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: Event-related fMRI within-subject design with specific timings for fixation, setup, punch line, rating, ISI, runs and breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example timings: 'Ready' fixation 8 s; setup displayed 14 s; punch line 9 s (setup remains visible so participants can integrate information); in-scan funniness rating 4 s; jittered ISI 3.1–9.9 s (mean 6.2 s); four runs of ~6 min 8 s each with up to three 2-min closed-eye breaks between runs; total experiment ~33 min. Randomize stimuli order to avoid response tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion criteria and ethical procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Define participant characteristics and ethical safeguards: age range, native language, handedness, informed consent, ethics approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: participants aged 21–30, native Chinese speakers, right-handed (Edinburgh Handedness Inventory), written informed consent obtained, study approved by institutional Research Ethics Committee. Exclude participants based on motion or other acquisition problems (see motion criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters and hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify scanner, coil, sequences and parameter values for anatomical and functional imaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 3T Siemens Magnetom Skyra, 32-channel head coil; T1 3D-MPRAGE (TR=1560 ms, TE=3.68 ms, FA=15°, voxel 1×1×1 mm); T2 coronal view parameters; functional T2*-weighted EPI: TR=2000 ms, TE=24 ms, FA=90°, matrix 64×64, FOV 256×256 mm, 34 axial slices thickness 3 mm (voxel ~4×4×3 mm), no gap; align to AC–PC line to capture whole brain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing pipeline (slice timing, realignment, coregistration, normalization, smoothing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard fMRI preprocessing steps to correct timing, motion, align anatomical-functional images, map to standard space, and increase SNR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slice-timing correction using interpolation (reference = first slice), realignment to correct head motion, co-registration of T1/T2/EPI, normalization to standardized EPI template (MNI coordinates) with segmentation if needed, and spatial smoothing using Gaussian kernel (8 mm FWHM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion exclusion threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude subject data if head motion exceeds a predefined threshold in translation or rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example rule: if head motion in any run > 1 voxel (~3 mm) in any of three translation parameters or exceeds rotation thresholds (x-y, y-z, x-z planes), remove the subject's data from analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: First- and second-level analysis procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Model event types at single-subject level and enter contrasts into group-level random-effects analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convolve onset functions with canonical HRF plus temporal derivative to capture BOLD latency variability; define contrasts (INS-RES minus NEU, ABS minus NEU, INS-RES minus ABS, ABS minus INS-RES); group-level: whole-brain random-effects analysis and paired-sample t-tests for main contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding non-independence in ROI analyses (split-half approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use independent data to define ROIs and to estimate effect sizes to prevent circular analysis ('double-dipping').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: use odd runs to identify candidate humor-processing regions and even runs to estimate BOLD signal change (Kriegeskorte et al., 2009). When using SVC, apply an a priori sphere (e.g., 8 mm radius) and appropriate thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical thresholding and cluster criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Define thresholds for reporting activations and to control for multiple comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example thresholds: illustrative peak threshold p < 0.001 (uncorrected); or voxel-level cluster threshold p < 0.05 FWE-corrected with minimum cluster size >= 10 voxels. Use z-scores and report MNI coordinates and cluster extents for contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral statistical analysis (ANOVA, post-hoc tests, effect sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze rating data with repeated-measures ANOVA and follow-ups to compare conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: one-way repeated-measures ANOVA across conditions for surprise, comprehensibility, funniness; use Bonferroni post-hoc tests for pairwise comparisons; report F, p, and effect size (η^2). Interpret patterns consistent with hypotheses (e.g., INC-RES > ABS > NEU for funniness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Neural mapping: regions implicated in incongruity detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detecting incongruities engages temporal and frontal language/semantic areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported detection-related regions include middle temporal gyrus (MTG) and middle frontal gyrus (MFG), left MFG/MTG activation common to both humor types for incongruity detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neural mapping: regions implicated in incongruity resolution (INS-RES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete semantic integration and perspective-taking processes engage temporo-parietal and medial parietal regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key regions: temporo-parietal junction (TPJ) and inferior parietal lobe (IPL) for multisensory integration/coherence building; precuneus for perspective taking; posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) and parahippocampal gyrus (PHG) for episodic memory retrieval and affective elaboration; SFG/MFG for higher-order reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neural mapping: regions implicated in partial resolution / absurd humor (ABS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial/pseudo-resolution relies more on word-level processing and pragmatic awareness areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported regions: fusiform gyrus and lingual gyrus (visual/word-form processing), inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) for phonological/semantic processing, and superior temporal gyrus (STG) for pragmatic awareness/meta-comprehension. These regions show stronger activation for ABS vs INS-RES.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of elaboration/affective stage (amusement intensity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to elaborate on protagonist traits and retrieve episodic memories mediates strength of amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incongruity-resolution humor permits elaboration (derogation, self-comparison), recruiting PCC and PHG and producing stronger funniness ratings; absurd humor lacks coherent protagonist elaboration, eliciting weaker amusement or confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast logic and reporting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use subtraction contrasts (e.g., INS-RES minus NEU) and direct contrasts (INS-RES vs ABS) and report both to localize type-specific activations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both simple contrasts against neutral baselines and direct differential contrasts; report peak coordinates, BA, voxel counts, z-scores, and cluster extents; visualizations (figures) to show enhanced BOLD activation for contrasts.
